alternatives.mechanism: Wrap the edit command in a shell function that first creates an atomic backup using a safe timestamp format and then launches the editor
addresses_issues: User forgets to run tool (the wrapper is invoked automatically when editing)
Timestamp format sanitized to avoid illegal characters
Backup performed via copy‑then‑rename to make it atomic
tradeoffs: Requires users to adopt the wrapper or alias
Adds a small overhead before opening the editor
Only works when the wrapper is used, not for external editors
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Uses a shell wrapper to embed backup creation into the edit workflow, eliminating manual step.

alternatives.mechanism: Deploy a lightweight file‑system watcher (e.g., inotify on Linux, FSEvents on macOS, ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows) that watches the target file and automatically creates a timestamped backup whenever the file is opened for write
addresses_issues: Eliminates reliance on user to remember to run the tool
Generates timestamp using ISO‑8601 without ':' to stay legal
Creates backup by copying to a temp file then renaming, ensuring atomicity
tradeoffs: Requires a background process to stay running
May generate backups for unintended writes (e.g., autosave)
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Introduces an always‑on watcher that autonomously backs up on write events.

alternatives.mechanism: Integrate the backup step into the file‑save operation via a custom editor plugin (e.g., a Vim/VSCode extension) that, on save, copies the file to a backup directory with a sanitized timestamp and uses atomic rename
addresses_issues: User cannot forget because backup is tied to save action
Timestamp format can be controlled to avoid illegal characters
Atomic rename ensures backup is not left corrupted
tradeoffs: Requires installing and configuring the plugin for each editor
Limited to editors that support extensions
Adds slight delay on each save
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Leverages editor extensibility to embed backup creation directly into the save lifecycle.
